provider.notes: Registered as google with no aliases (gateway/src/plugin/builtin/mod.rs:74-84, :1669-1671; gateway/src/core/stt/standard.rs:428). The client speaks only the gRPC StreamingRecognize method of Speech-to-Text V2 (gateway/src/core/stt/google/provider.rs:185) and copies the model string to the request unchanged (gateway/src/core/stt/google/streaming.rs:249); it has no model, region or language check. default_model is latest_long because that is the default the client declares (gateway/src/core/stt/google/config.rs:122). It is a lookup key only. The constructor paths pass an empty model to Google as an empty string (gateway/src/core/stt/google/provider.rs:464-477; gateway/src/core/stt/base.rs:592), so a session with no model does not send latest_long today, and what Google does with an empty model on the implicit recognizer is unverified (the audit inferred that Google rejects it). If the resolver writes this default into the request it changes the wire for those sessions and needs its own test. The client dials the recognizer location global unless the session supplies provider_extras.location on the standardized path (gateway/src/core/stt/google/config.rs:7, :126, :175-177); the flat constructor path cannot set a location. Model availability depends on the recognizer location (global, us, eu or a region) and, for chirp_2, on the language. The chirp_2 language limit is a constraint on its streaming transport; locations are not written as constraints, because Google's sources disagree and a wrong constraint would refuse sessions that work (Google names its Locations API as the live source). Every final from this client is marked speech-final, so Google's own finalization ends the utterance on the streaming path. The client has no handling for a model that ends the stream after every utterance (latest_short, and probably short): each close is treated as a dropped stream and uses up the reconnect budget, which is why the latest_short streaming client is marked known broken. Not listed as a transport: BatchRecognize, an asynchronous job that reads only from Cloud Storage.

The model string reaches Google unchanged, and a model Google rejects surfaces through the error callback after connect() has already reported success (provider.rs:96-104, inferred from reading), not as a setup failure. Google closes a stream after 5 minutes with the documented error '409 Max duration of 5 minutes reached for stream'; the client has no rotation timer and relies on a reactive reconnect. That error most likely arrives as the gRPC code ABORTED, which the client treats as reconnectable (provider.rs:251-264; the mapping from 409 to ABORTED is inferred and was not probed). The pinned protocol definitions (google-api-proto 1.678.0, gateway/Cargo.toml:279) lack this model's endpointing_sensitivity and custom_prompt_config fields, so neither can be sent. The client dials the recognizer location global unless the session supplies provider_extras.location (gateway/src/core/stt/google/config.rs:7, :175-177); the flat constructor path cannot set one (gateway/src/core/stt/google/provider.rs:464-477). Google's sources disagree on whether global serves this model, so a session that leaves the location unset may be rejected by Google; this has not been probed.

gateway_client.defect: Google closes the stream on this model after every utterance, and the gateway's Google client has no single-utterance handling. It treats each close as a dropped stream, records a failure on the circuit breaker that every Google session shares, and reconnects after a delay that grows with each attempt. The retry budget is ten attempts and is cleared only when a stream has stayed open for 30 seconds, so a call whose caller speaks more often than that loses transcription after about ten utterances. Three closes in a row within 5 seconds of their connect put the shared breaker in its fatal state for 60 seconds, which also stops other Google sessions from connecting. All of this is read in the code and was never run against Google. Until the client treats the per-utterance close as normal, a model that keeps the stream open (long, latest_long, telephony) is the better choice.
gateway_client.code_ref: gateway/src/core/stt/google/provider.rs:219-228 (a stream that ends is returned as a reconnectable failure); gateway/src/core/stt/google/streaming.rs:267-271 (the streaming features sent have no single-utterance field); gateway/src/core/websocket/reconnectable_stream.rs:294, :353-361 and :387-405 (each cycle counts one attempt and one breaker failure, and the attempt counter is cleared only after a stream outlived reset_after_ms); gateway/src/core/websocket/reconnection.rs:99-108 (ten attempts, 30 000 ms); gateway/src/core/resilience/circuit_breaker.rs:101-112, :247-267 and :334-367 (three consecutive streams shorter than 5 seconds arm a fatal state that refuses connects for 60 seconds); gateway/src/core/resilience/registry.rs:103-108 (one breaker per provider, default settings); gateway/tests/mock_endpoint_e2e.rs:2301 (the only test, against a mock that does not close per utterance)
gateway_client.notes: The adapter itself is exercised against an in-repo gRPC mock, but not with this model's behaviour. The vendor audit lists latest_short on a call with several turns among the combinations the client accepts and cannot serve. A single-utterance use (one spoken command, then hang up) works today; a conversation does not. The effect on the shared breaker is inferred from reading; because it also stops other Google sessions from connecting, the client fix matters beyond this model.

provenance.notes: Google documents that a stream on this model is closed automatically when the utterance ends. The model streams at the vendor, but the gateway's client cannot run it on a call with several turns: today such a session starts, transcribes the first utterances with a reconnect between each, and then stops transcribing. Following decisions section 15, the streaming client is marked known broken and stays usable with a warning, which keeps single-utterance uses working; it is listed behind the Recognize transport (conversion rules section 9), which takes over from Release 5 once a live probe confirms that Recognize accepts this model (its disabled_reason). The streaming method is the only one Google documents for this id.
